narratives.strongestCounter: In this file 12 of 21 decided scheme-election pairs ended in the incumbent losing with the scheme live (AP 2024, TG 2023, OR 2024, CT 2023, RJ 2023, DL 2025, KL 2026, TN 2011, TN 2026); the two pre-poll waivers by incumbents (Raje 2018, Siddaramaiah 2017) both lost; challengers won on promises, not transfers; no opened Lokniti cross-tab isolates a beneficiary effect.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: A post-poll survey cross-tab (beneficiary vs eligible non-beneficiary) with a vote gap ≥10 points in two states, or a regression-discontinuity on payment timing (e.g. KALIA batches Jan–May 2019 vs booth-level BJD swing).

narratives.claim: The 2018 farm loan waivers were fiscally reckless and poorly targeted
narratives.strongestCase: RBI IWG: Rs 2.4 lakh cr since 2014-15, only ~66% reached banks, credit culture damaged; Maharashtra 2017 left Rs 5,976 cr undelivered on its own page; Karnataka 2018 left 30,733 farmers unpaid five years on; UP's Rs 36,000 cr covered a third of farm debt.
narratives.strongestCounter: Waivers responded to a real 2017–18 distress cycle (Shekhawati, Maharashtra strikes); official outturns (MH Rs 18,762 cr; MH 2019 Rs 20,497 cr) show money did reach tens of lakhs of accounts.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: CAG state-level audits of the 2017–19 waivers (none opened this session).

narratives.claim: Timing of Kerala's pension arrears payments was election-driven
narratives.strongestCase: Two months' dues released three weeks before the Apr 2024 LS poll after five months of default; CPI(M) itself named the default as a cause of the 19–1 LS defeat; the five-instalment schedule was set to end in 2025-26, the pre-assembly fiscal year.
narratives.strongestCounter: The CM's borrowing-limit account (KIIFB/KSSPL reclassification, divisible-pool cut) is on the record and partly corroborated by CAG/PRS notes on off-budget borrowing.
narratives.whatWouldChangeThis: KSSPL monthly cash-flow and borrowing-window data showing releases tracked liquidity, not the calendar.

symmetryCheck: Same lens on every party. Pre-poll launch/hike by an incumbent within 12 months: BRS (Rythu Bandhu 2018), BJD (KALIA 2019), AAP (Delhi 200 units 2019), BJP (Raje Rs 50,000 waiver 2018; Kanya Sumangala budget 2019), INC (Siddaramaiah Rs 50,000 waiver 2017), TMC (Kanyashree universalisation 2019), CPI(M)/LDF (pension arrears tranches 2024, 2025-26). Post-poll delivery of a promise: BJP (UP 2017, MH 2017), INC (PB 2017, MP/CT/RJ 2018, KA 2023, TG 2024), JD(S)-INC (KA 2018), Shiv Sena-led MVA (MH 2019), DMK (TV 2006, bus 2021), AIADMK (mixie 2011), AAP (PB power 2022), JD(U) (cycle 2006). Audit findings of leakage: BJD (KALIA, CAG), BRS (Aasara, CAG; Rythu Bandhu, IGIDR), INC (Karnataka fiscal strain, CAG), DMK (TV reconciliation, IndiaSpend). Promise exceeding delivery: INC (Anna Bhagya 10 kg → 5 kg + cash for 19 months; Rythu Bharosa Rs 15,000 promised → Rs 12,000 paid), BJP (MH 2017 Rs 5,976 cr undelivered; UP waiver a third of farm debt per Congress), JD(S)-INC (30,733 farmers unpaid five years on), BJD (3 of 5 KALIA instalments), LDF (five months of pensions unpaid). Cuts by successors: JD(S) cut Anna Bhagya 7 kg → 5 kg (2018); AIADMK scrapped the TV scheme (2011); Congress excluded non-agricultural land from Rythu Bharosa (2025). Continuations by rivals: BJP kept Delhi power (2025) and Chiranjeevi (2024); TDP kept and rebadged YSR schemes; BJP replaced KALIA with a cash scheme of its own. The PM's July 2022 "revdi" speech sits beside: UP 2017 waiver (BJP), Gujarat's Rs 12,207 cr farm power subsidy (BJP), Delhi BJP continuing 200 free units (2025), Raje's pre-poll waiver (2018). Outcome symmetry: incumbents with live schemes lost in 12 of 21 decided pairs, spread across BRS, YSRCP, BJD, INC, AAP, DMK, LDF and BJP (CT 2018); no party's scheme in this file reliably preceded a win.
